sql:
SELECT count(*) AS customers_without_orders
FROM customer c
WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM orders o WHERE o.o_custkey = c.c_custkey)

extra.AI Reason: The query counts rows from the customer table that do not have a corresponding entry in the orders table using an Anti Join.
A Hash Anti Join is the most efficient way to filter out customers that have orders.
Full scan of the customer table is required to check all customers.
Build a hash table on the orders table to perform the anti-join.
Full scan of the orders table to build the hash table.

differences.text: PostgreSQL runs part of the plan in parallel (Gather), with partial aggregation in each worker. The AI plan runs in a single process.
Hash Join of (orders, customer): PostgreSQL hashes (customer). The AI hashes (orders). PostgreSQL usually hashes the smaller input.
Join of (orders, customer): PostgreSQL performs a Right Anti join, the AI an Anti join.
Hash: PostgreSQL applies it to (customer), the AI to (orders).

Table customer: PostgreSQL uses Index Only Scan on customer using customer_pkey. The AI uses Seq Scan on customer. A sequential scan wins when many rows qualify. An index scan wins when few rows qualify. A bitmap scan sits in between. The AI's reason: "Full scan of the customer table is required to check all customers."
Only the PostgreSQL plan has Gather over (orders, customer) (collects rows from parallel worker processes).
Only the PostgreSQL plan has Aggregate (Plain, Partial) over (orders, customer) (computes aggregates (GROUP BY, SUM, COUNT, ...)).

similarities: Both plans join the tables in the same order (every intermediate join result is the same).
Both plans use Seq Scan on orders.
